extracted.intended_audience: software developers and repository reviewers using GitHub pull requests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing code reviews on GitHub pull requests: understanding intent, examining diffs/files, leaving line-level comments or suggestions, using tools like Copilot and Codespaces, and submitting an overall review decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review files one at a time
rubrics_metrics.description: It's best to review changes in a pull request one file at a time: Examine each individual file changed in the pull request. Leave comments on specific changes. After reviewing a file, mark it as Viewed to collapse it and track your progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The progress bar in the pull request header shows how many files you've viewed. Marking files as viewed collapses them; if a file changes after you view it, it will be unmarked as viewed. Use this workflow to keep reviews focused and manageable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the purpose and motivation of the pull request
rubrics_metrics.description: Gaining a clear understanding of the motivation behind a pull request helps inform your review, so you can keep it targeted and meaningful, and provide feedback that is aligned with the pull request author’s intent and the project's goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use context such as linked issues/discussions, linked projects/milestones (from the pull request sidebar) to frame your review and check alignment with original intent. Ask questions like 'What problem does this pull request solve?' or 'How does this PR relate to issue ISSUE-URL?'. This contextual understanding should guide where to focus line-level review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the pull request sidebar context (issues, discussions, projects, milestones)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the pull request sidebar, you can find valuable context including linked issues or discussions and linked projects or milestones to understand problems, goals, background, design decisions, or current debates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review linked issues/discussions to gather background information; review linked projects/milestones to see how the PR fits within larger work or releases. Use that context to check if PR goals align with original intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Copilot Chat to clarify intent and summarize changes
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask Copilot Chat for help understanding the pull request’s intent or for clarification on any part of the change; Copilot Chat can help clarify the bigger picture before diving into line-level review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Copilot Chat from the top right, with PR attached to the prompt. Example prompts: 'What problem does this pull request solve?', 'Why were these changes needed?', 'Summarize the goals of this PR based on the linked issue.' You can also ask Copilot about individual commits (e.g., 'Summarize the changes in this commit', 'Who committed these changes?'). If you know a commit SHA, include it in the prompt. Note: you'll need access to GitHub Copilot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configure diff view and file filters for effective review
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the format of the diff view (unified or split) and hide whitespace differences as needed; optionally filter the files to show only the files you want to review or use the file tree to navigate to a specific file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click the diff view control to choose unified or split; the choice is remembered per user for future PRs. Hiding whitespace differences can reduce noise. For more complex PRs, filter files to focus on relevant subsets (see 'Filtering files in a pull request'). Always consider switching views or filters if the default view obscures important changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add line-level comments and suggestions correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Hover over the line of code where you'd like to add a comment, click the blue comment icon, or select a range of lines to comment on multiple lines. Optionally, suggest a specific change by using the suggestion block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To select multiple lines, click the first line number and drag or Shift+click the last. Use the suggestion feature: click the suggestion icon, edit the text within the suggestion block, and include ```suggestion to explain changes where appropriate. To add a comment directly on a file, use the file-level comment control. Use specific, actionable comments rather than vague criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start, manage, and abandon a review (pending comments workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: When you're done adding review comments, click Start a review to begin a review session. Pending comments are only visible to you until you submit the review. You can edit pending comments anytime before submission. To cancel a pending review, including all pending comments, use Abandon review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you've already started a review, use Add review comment to add more. Remember pending comments are private until you submit; use that to curate and aggregate feedback. To cancel everything you added during a review session, select Review changes then Abandon review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use suggestions that authors can apply directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Optionally, to suggest a specific change that the author can click to commit if they agree, use the 'Make a Suggestion' flow which copies selected lines into the comment box for editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click and hold the + sign next to the first line, drag to the last line, then click Make a Suggestion in the comment box. The suggested lines are editable; prefix explanatory notes with a ```suggestion block if desired. This makes it easy for authors to accept small fixes directly from the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test and review changes using GitHub Codespaces when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use GitHub Codespaces to test, run, and review pull requests by opening the PR in a codespace and using the GitHub Pull Request view to open files and add review comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open the pull request in a codespace (see 'Using GitHub Codespaces for pull requests'). In the Codespaces Activity Bar, use the GitHub Pull Request view and click the Open File icon to inspect code. Add comments via the + icon next to line numbers, and use Start Review or Make a Suggestion as usual. Codespaces lets you run and test code for higher-confidence reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review dependency changes and check for security issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If the pull request contains changes to dependencies, use the dependency review for a manifest or lock file to see what has changed and check whether the changes introduce security vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the Files changed tab, open the dependency review for manifest/lock files using the rich diff button on the right of the header. Also review the source diff because some changes to manifest/lock files may not change dependencies, or GitHub might not parse certain dependencies. Use the source diff button to return to the source view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark files as viewed to track progress
rubrics_metrics.description: After you finish reviewing a file, mark the file as Viewed so it collapses and you can track which files remain to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the Files changed tab, click Viewed on the right of the file header after finishing. Note that if the file changes after you viewed it, it will be unmarked as viewed, indicating you should re-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit your review with a summary and appropriate verdict
rubrics_metrics.description: After finishing the files you want to review, submit your review by typing a summarizing comment and selecting Comment, Approve, or Request changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose: Comment to leave general feedback without approving or blocking; Approve to submit positive feedback and indicate readiness to merge; Request changes to submit feedback that must be addressed before the PR should be merged (see branch protection notes). Click Submit review to make the review public. Your summary should provide actionable, prioritized guidance rather than only line-level comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand review outcomes, branch-protection, and merge semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Know that the Request changes option is informational and will not prevent merging unless branch protection (or a ruleset) is configured to require pull request reviews. Repository owners/administrators can merge without approvals. Approvals can be dismissed by new commits and approvals are grouped by permission level when required reviews are configured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required reviews and stale review dismissal are enabled and a code-modifying commit is pushed to the branch of an approved PR, the approval is dismissed and the PR must be re-reviewed. When multiple PRs point to the same commit, you may be blocked from merging if one has a pending/rejected review. If your repository requires approvals from people with write/admin permissions, the reviewers sidebar groups approvals by permission level: top section counts toward merge requirements; collapsible section shows other approvals. Pull request authors (and Copilot-assigned authors in some cases) cannot approve their own PRs. Repository owners and admins can still merge regardless of review state unless rules prevent it.
